nindian-polity-67-28.s: Which of the following doctrine – case pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Doctrine of Pith and Substance – State of Rajasthan v. G. Chawla
Doctrine of Colourable Legislation – Kameshwar Singh v. State of Bihar
nindian-polity-67-28.x: The Doctrine of Eclipse comes from Bhikaji Narain Dhakras v. State of M.P.; Prafulla Kumar is a pith and substance case.

nd4a7821504e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Article 254(2)?
o: A repugnant State law on a Concurrent List subject prevails in that State if it receives the President's assent
Such a State law, once assented to, prevails throughout India
Parliament can later amend or repeal such a State law by a fresh law
The State law must be reserved for the consideration of the President
nd4a7821504e.x: A State law assented to under Article 254(2) prevails only in that State, not throughout India.

nf354af8c197.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Article 252?
o: Two or more State Legislatures must pass resolutions requesting parliamentary legislation
Any other State may adopt the law later by a resolution of its legislature
The requesting State Legislatures may independently repeal the law
Only Parliament can amend or repeal a law made under it
nf354af8c197.x: Only Parliament can amend or repeal a law enacted under Article 252; the requesting States cannot repeal it on their own.

n99162de7391.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the territorial extent of laws?
o: Parliament may make laws for the whole or any part of India
A parliamentary law is not invalid merely because it has extra-territorial operation
A State law needs a sufficient territorial nexus for extra-territorial reach
A State Legislature may ordinarily legislate for another State's territory without any territorial connection
n99162de7391.x: A State law requires a sufficient territorial nexus for any extra-territorial reach, so the last statement is false.

nindian-polity-68-33.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Article 249 – Rajya Sabha resolution in national interest
Article 252 – Rajya Sabha resolution in national interest
Article 356 – Proclamation of President's Rule in a State
nindian-polity-68-33.x: Article 252 is triggered by a request of two or more State Legislatures; the Rajya Sabha resolution in national interest is Article 249.

nea64dff636d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about preservation of livestock (cow slaughter)?
o: Parliament may legislate on it only through the ordinary Union List power
Preservation of livestock is a State List subject
Article 48 is relevant to constitutional policy on preservation of livestock
Parliament can legislate on it through Articles 249, 250 or 252
nea64dff636d.x: Being a State subject, Parliament can legislate on it through routes such as Articles 249, 250 or 252, not through the ordinary Union List power.

nd6c6f5eaf22.s: Under Article 246(4), Parliament may legislate for areas not included in a State (Union Territories) on matters in:
o: The Union and Concurrent Lists only
nd6c6f5eaf22.x: Article 246(4) lets Parliament legislate for areas not included in a State on matters in all three Lists, not merely the Union List.

nb1689335247.s: Repugnancy between Union and State laws is dealt with by Article:
nb1689335247.x: Article 254 deals with repugnancy; Article 255 concerns recommendations and previous sanctions as procedural matters, and Article 248 with residuary powers.

nindian-polity-68-5.s: Education was moved from the State List to the Concurrent List by the:
nindian-polity-68-5.x: The 42nd Amendment (1976) moved Education from the State List to the Concurrent List.

n4fd1e308c1f.s: Preventive detention for reasons connected with security of a State and public order falls under the:
n4fd1e308c1f.x: Concurrent List Entry 3 covers preventive detention for State security and public order, while Union List Entry 9 covers it for defence, foreign affairs and security of India.

ncd63d15e6ff.s: The scheme of distribution of legislative powers in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the constitution of:
ncd63d15e6ff.x: India's scheme of legislative distribution follows the Canadian model.

n5e7997b62ef.s: A Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249 remains in force for a period not exceeding:
n5e7997b62ef.x: An Article 249 resolution lasts up to one year and may be renewed any number of times, one year at a time.

nd4f74c455da.s: The Transplantation of Human Organs Act, 1994 was enacted by Parliament under Article:
nd4f74c455da.x: It is an example of a law made by Parliament under Article 252 following resolutions by two or more State Legislatures.

nindian-polity-68-4.s: Under Article 246, legislative competence over the Concurrent List rests with:
o: Parliament only during a National Emergency
nindian-polity-68-4.x: Under Article 246, Parliament alone legislates on the Union List, States on the State List, and both on the Concurrent List.

nindian-polity-67-13.s: Judicial review by the higher judiciary tests the constitutional validity of:
o: Both legislative acts and executive actions
nindian-polity-67-13.x: Judicial review is the higher judiciary's power to test both laws and executive action.

nindian-polity-68-51.s: Parliament exercises the legislative powers of a State Legislature during President's Rule under Article:
nindian-polity-68-51.x: Under Article 356 Parliament exercises the State Legislature's powers; Article 250 applies during a National Emergency and Article 252 on request of two or more States.

nindian-polity-68-13.s: A law made by Parliament on a State List subject under Article 250 ceases to have effect ____ after the National Emergency ends.
nindian-polity-68-13.x: Laws made under Article 250 lapse six months after the Emergency ends.

nindian-polity-67-25.s: 'What cannot be done directly cannot be done indirectly' is the principle behind the Doctrine of:
nindian-polity-67-25.x: This maxim underlies the doctrine of colourable legislation, which checks whether a legislature crosses its competence under a permissible guise.

nindian-polity-67-7.s: A pre-Constitution law that conflicts with a Fundamental Right stays dormant and revives if that right is amended. This is the Doctrine of:
nindian-polity-67-7.x: Under the doctrine of eclipse such a law is not dead ab initio but only overshadowed, and it revives when the right is amended.

n7db25aaccd0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the executive power of the Union?
o: It may be exercised directly by the President
It may be exercised through subordinate officers
The President's power as Supreme Commander is not subject to regulation by law
The President is the Supreme Commander of the armed forces
n7db25aaccd0.x: The President's power as Supreme Commander of the armed forces is regulated by law.

nad3b4604607.shape: one-liner (NOT not possible: the original has no false statement)
nad3b4604607.s: Failure of a State to comply with Union directions may be treated as a breakdown of constitutional machinery under Article:
nad3b4604607.x: Article 365 allows such non-compliance to be treated as a breakdown of constitutional machinery, opening the way to action under Article 356.

n4f3f7ffd1c4.s: Under Article 356, the powers of which of the following remain untouched when President's Rule is imposed in a State?
n4f3f7ffd1c4.x: Article 356 expressly leaves the powers of the State High Court untouched; the President takes over the executive and the Council of Ministers is dismissed.

ne2bfb82a0c9.s: Under Article 73, the executive power of the Union extends to matters on which ____ can make laws.
ne2bfb82a0c9.x: Article 73 extends Union executive power to matters on which Parliament can legislate and to rights and authority under treaties or agreements.

ne6832244be9.s: Article 239AA, giving Delhi a Legislative Assembly and a Council of Ministers, was inserted by the:
ne6832244be9.x: The 69th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1991 inserted Article 239AA.

nf12dac7cba9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sarkaria Commission?
o: It was set up in June 1983 under Justice R.S. Sarkaria
It recommended a temporary Inter-State Council convened only during emergencies
It recommended that Article 356 be used sparingly
nf12dac7cba9.x: The Sarkaria Commission recommended a permanent Inter-State Council, not a temporary one.

nbf2ce1eaf30.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about inter-State water disputes?
o: The Mullaperiyar dam is located on the Godavari river
The Mahanadi dispute is between Odisha and Chhattisgarh
The Mullaperiyar dam is situated in Kerala
The Mullaperiyar dam is operated by Tamil Nadu under a lease
nbf2ce1eaf30.x: Mullaperiyar is on the Periyar, not the Godavari.

n833090823f0.s:
Assertion (A): Advisers such as Chief Secretaries have voting rights in the Zonal Councils.
Reason (R): Each member State is represented in its Zonal Council by its Chief Minister and two Ministers.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n833090823f0.x: Advisers such as Chief Secretaries attend without voting rights, so A is false; R correctly states the State representation.

n22bb7496cb5.s: The Indian Forest Service, an All India Service, was created in:
n22bb7496cb5.x: The Indian Forest Service was created in 1966; it is an All India Service along with the IAS and IPS.

nf5da0c320d0.s: Officers of the All India Services are recruited on an all-India basis by the:
nf5da0c320d0.x: UPSC recruits them; the Centre trains them and they serve in State cadres.

n036948567f9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 80th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000?
o: It gave effect to the Tenth Finance Commission's 'Alternative Scheme of Devolution'
It was made effective from 1 April 2000
It omitted Article 272 on sharing of Union excise duties
It made the States share the gross proceeds of all Union taxes
n036948567f9.x: Though enacted in 2000, the 80th Amendment was made effective from 1 April 1996.

n43a24c195a5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
o: It retained the vertical share of States in the divisible pool at 41%
The Union Government accepted this recommendation in Budget 2026–27
Distribution of the divisible pool among individual States is inter se devolution
Vertical share refers to distribution of the divisible pool among individual States
n43a24c195a5.x: Vertical devolution concerns the Centre–State share; distribution among individual States is inter se (horizontal) devolution.

nindian-polity-61-18.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Article 265 – No tax except by authority of law
Article 266 – Consolidated Funds and Public Accounts
Article 268 – Contingency Fund of a State
nindian-polity-61-18.x: Article 268 deals with duties levied by the Union but collected by the States; Contingency Funds are under Article 267.

nc0265126b0e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about grants-in-aid?
o: Statutory grants under Article 275 are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
Statutory grants are made on the recommendation of NITI Aayog
Discretionary grants under Article 282 may be made for any public purpose
Statutory grants are made on the recommendation of the Finance Commission
nc0265126b0e.x: Statutory grants under Article 275 are made on the recommendation of the Finance Commission, not NITI Aayog.

n9b83026e556.s: Under Article 269, taxes on inter-State sale or purchase of goods (other than newspapers) are:
o: Levied and collected by the States and appropriated by them
Levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States
Levied, collected and appropriated exclusively by the Union
Levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States
n9b83026e556.x: Under Article 269 the Union levies and collects these taxes (including taxes on consignment of goods) and assigns them to the States.

n0e2ce4b95e6.s: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) is a ____-based tax.
n0e2ce4b95e6.x: GST is a destination-based tax that subsumed about 17 earlier taxes.

n5c1841ee5d5.s: Corporation tax, levied and collected by the Union, has been shared with the States since the:
n5c1841ee5d5.x: Since the 80th Constitutional Amendment, corporation tax is part of the shareable pool of Union taxes.

n10c0888cc7f.s: Under Article 268 (e.g. stamp duties on specified instruments), duties are:
o: Levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States
Levied and collected by the States but appropriated by the Union
Levied by the States and collected jointly by the Union and the States
Levied, collected and appropriated exclusively by the Union
n10c0888cc7f.x: Article 268 covers duties levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States.

n4d632a423b5.s: Under Article 246A, the power to make GST laws on inter-State supplies rests exclusively with:
n4d632a423b5.x: Article 246A gives concurrent GST power to Parliament and State Legislatures, but Parliament alone legislates on inter-State supplies.

nindian-polity-2-53.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Article 359 – Duty of the Union to protect the States
Article 354 – Distribution of revenues during an Emergency
Article 355 – Duty of the Union to protect the States
Article 358 – Suspension of Article 19 during an Emergency
nindian-polity-2-53.x: Article 359 deals with suspension of enforcement of Fundamental Rights; the Union's duty to protect the States is Article 355.

nb0c49a19a7c.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Inter-State water dispute tribunals – Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956
nb0c49a19a7c.x: State consent for CBI investigation is governed by Section 6 of the DSPE Act, not Article 156, which concerns the Governor.

n4e8fbdbac25.s:
Assertion (A): The Polavaram project is 100% funded by the Centre.
Reason (R): Polavaram has been declared a national project under Section 90 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n4e8fbdbac25.x: Polavaram is a national project under Section 90 (not 89) of APRA 2014, and as a national project it is fully Centre-funded.

n1a4ec15ef4d.s: Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh was promised in Parliament by Prime Minister:
n1a4ec15ef4d.x: Manmohan Singh promised SCS in Parliament, but the promise was never written into the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.

nbbf05c58b26.s: Which of the following is NOT a principle laid down in S.R. Bommai v. Union of India?
o: A proclamation under Article 356 is subject to judicial review
The Governor's opinion is the conclusive test of majority in the Assembly
The floor test in the Assembly is the proper test of majority
A court can restore a dismissed State government in an appropriate case
nbbf05c58b26.x: Bommai held that the Governor's opinion is not conclusive; majority must ordinarily be tested on the floor of the Assembly.

nindian-polity-44-26.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Parliamentary approval of National Emergency – 1 month
Renewal cycle of an approved National Emergency – 6 months
Parliamentary approval of President's Rule – 1 month
Maximum duration of President's Rule with extensions – 3 years
nindian-polity-44-26.x: President's Rule must be approved by Parliament within two months; one month applies to a National Emergency.

nindian-polity-50-38.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Articles 358 and 359?
o: Article 358 automatically suspends the freedoms under Article 19
Article 358 operates when the Emergency is proclaimed on the ground of armed rebellion
Article 359 requires a specific, separate Presidential Order
Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended
nindian-polity-50-38.x: Article 358 does not apply to an Emergency proclaimed on the ground of armed rebellion.

n1a78129ded3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about parliamentary approval of a National Emergency?
o: Approval requires only a simple majority in each House
Both Houses must approve the proclamation within one month
Once approved, it continues for six months
It can be extended indefinitely with approval every six months
n1a78129ded3.x: Approval of a National Emergency needs a special majority in each House; simple majority applies to a Financial Emergency.

nae152c777a1.s: If one-tenth of Lok Sabha members give notice, a special sitting to consider disapproval of a National Emergency must be held within:
nae152c777a1.x: Notice by one-tenth of Lok Sabha members requires a special sitting within 14 days.

n2693e86d7b8.s: In which case did the Supreme Court affirm that a proclamation of National Emergency under Article 352 is reviewable?
n2693e86d7b8.x: Minerva Mills affirmed reviewability, reversing the 38th Amendment's attempt to make the President's satisfaction non-justiciable.

n764cc85a0dc.s: Article 358 automatically suspends Article 19 when a National Emergency is proclaimed on the ground of:
n764cc85a0dc.x: Article 358 operates only for an Emergency based on war or external aggression, not armed rebellion.

nindian-polity-44-19.s: The maximum gap between two sessions of Parliament is governed by Article:
nindian-polity-44-19.x: Article 85 governs the session gap; Article 62(2) deals with a Presidential vacancy and Article 352 with National Emergency.

n61a863af946.s: Written advice of the Union Cabinet for proclaiming a National Emergency was made mandatory by the:
n61a863af946.x: Article 352(3), inserted by the 44th Amendment, makes written advice of the Union Cabinet mandatory.

n963bc545aae.s: Under Article 356, the President may impose President's Rule in a State:
o: Only on the report of the Governor
Only with the consent of the State Legislature
On the report of the Governor or otherwise
Only on a resolution of the Rajya Sabha
n963bc545aae.x: The President may act on the Governor's report or otherwise; State Legislature consent is not a precondition.

n86aad0bfb0b.s: During President's Rule, the State is administered on behalf of the President by the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
n86aad0bfb0b.x: The Governor administers the State on behalf of the President, Parliament legislates for it, and the High Court is unaffected.

n1fb64a76b33.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Articles 301 to 307?
o: Under Article 302, Parliament may restrict trade, commerce and intercourse in the public interest
Article 303 deals with preference or discrimination by the Union or States
Article 305 saves existing laws and State monopolies
Article 306 continues to operate as the principal provision for Part B States
n1fb64a76b33.x: Article 306, relating to Part B States, has been repealed.

n58a4b5e8259.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about inter-State river water disputes?
o: Under Article 262, Parliament may exclude the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and other courts
The Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 provides for tribunals
The Supreme Court's original jurisdiction under Article 131 covers all such disputes
Article 131 does not cover inter-State water disputes
n58a4b5e8259.x: Article 131 does not cover inter-State water disputes, since Article 262(2) lets Parliament bar court jurisdiction over them.

n716f806d024.s:
Assertion (A): Governors of all States are permanent members of the Inter-State Council.
Reason (R): Six Union Cabinet Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister are members of the Inter-State Council.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n716f806d024.x: Governors are included only for States under President's Rule, so A is false; R is true.

n220002a3a28.s: The Mahadayi Water Disputes Tribunal (2010) involves Goa, Karnataka and:
n220002a3a28.x: The Mahadayi Tribunal involves Goa, Karnataka and Maharashtra.

nc12fb9e0b9a.s: The Krishna River Management Board (KRMB) and Godavari River Management Board (GRMB) were set up under the:
nc12fb9e0b9a.x: KRMB and GRMB come from the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 and work with an Apex Council.

n0bc12957a31.s: The Vansadhara Water Disputes Tribunal was constituted in:
n0bc12957a31.x: The Vansadhara Tribunal dates from 2010; the Godavari and First Krishna Tribunals from 1969 and the Second Krishna Tribunal from 2004.

n9518a1cc295.s: The Standing Committee of the Inter-State Council is chaired by the:
n9518a1cc295.x: The Prime Minister chairs the Council, while the Union Home Minister chairs its Standing Committee.

n72cd2de799a.s: The Sarkaria Commission proposed constitutional status for a renamed National Economic and Development Council under Article:
n72cd2de799a.x: The NEDC was to get status under Article 263; Article 280 deals with the Finance Commission.

n3ad9f89cc01.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about All India Services and State autonomy?
o: All India Services have no role in Centre-State coordination
Officers are governed in important respects by Central rules
States cannot fully discipline or remove such officers
Officers are recruited by the UPSC but serve in the States
n3ad9f89cc01.x: All India Services are also defended as promoting Centre-State coordination.

na5efa37ac49.s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission?
o: Use of Article 356 very sparingly and as a last resort
Abolition of the All India Services
Consultation with States on laws relating to the Concurrent List
na5efa37ac49.x: The Sarkaria Commission favoured strengthening the All India Services, not abolishing them.

n92e40acd617.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about central agencies and State consent?
o: Under Section 6 of the DSPE Act, 1946, the CBI needs State consent to act in a State
The NIA can investigate scheduled offences without State consent
The NIA functions under the NIA Act, 2008
The Enforcement Directorate needs a State's general consent to enforce PMLA and FEMA there
n92e40acd617.x: The ED enforces PMLA, 2002 and FEMA, 1999 nationwide with no State consent needed.

n2aaed8273a5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the State autonomy debate in India?
o: Autonomy demands grew after the Congress lost power in many States in the mid-1960s
The Punjab militancy of the 1980s is cited in favour of greater State autonomy
Coalition politics after the 1990s led towards more cooperative federalism
The Punjab militancy of the 1980s is cited to stress national unity
n2aaed8273a5.x: The Punjab militancy is cited against greater autonomy, stressing unity.

n66bf828c34d.s:
Assertion (A): A new All India Service can be created after the Lok Sabha passes a resolution supported by two-thirds of members present and voting.
Reason (R): All India Service officers are recruited by the UPSC but serve the States.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n66bf828c34d.x: The resolution must be passed by the Rajya Sabha, not the Lok Sabha, so A is false; R is true.

n6c028eb4f53.s: The demand to restrict the Centre to defence, foreign affairs, currency and communications was specifically associated with:
n6c028eb4f53.x: This four-subject demand is associated with Punjab and West Bengal; Tamil Nadu's position sought deletion of Article 356 and abolition of the All India Services and Planning Commission.

n7aef1e99e6e.s: Special Category Status, not provided for in the Constitution, was granted to States by the:
n7aef1e99e6e.x: SCS was granted by the National Development Council using the Gadgil formula criteria.

na511993e6d5.s: The study team on Centre-State relations of the Administrative Reforms Commission (1966) was headed by:
na511993e6d5.x: M.C. Setalvad headed the study team; the ARC itself was chaired first by Morarji Desai and later by K. Hanumanthaiya.

nbac55bed984.s: Which of the following is NOT cited as contributing to centralisation in contemporary federalism debates?
nbac55bed984.x: State Finance Commissions strengthen local fiscal devolution; cesses, CSS and GST are cited in the centralisation critique.

ncc41ed85a80.s: Articles 256, 257, 365 and ____ are criticised in federalism debates as instruments of Union overreach.
ncc41ed85a80.x: Articles 356, 256, 257 and 365 are identified as provisions that may enable excessive Union intervention.

nae19c3d11bf.s: Which body proposed the concept of a 'localised emergency'?
nae19c3d11bf.x: The Punchhi Commission proposed the localised emergency; Rajamannar sought deletion of Article 356 and Sarkaria treated it as a last resort.

n31f87331dac.s: The coalition era, giving the States a greater say in Centre-State relations, began in the:
n31f87331dac.x: Congress dominance marked the 1950s and early 1960s, opposition State governments rose from the mid-1960s, and the coalition era began in the 1990s.

n9a0e578e30c.s: Under Special Category Status, the Central share in funding of plan spending was:
n9a0e578e30c.x: SCS involved 90 per cent Central funding of plan spending; the 14th Finance Commission instead raised devolution to 42 per cent and used revenue deficit grants.

n429992e4ff4.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Rajamannar Committee?
o: It was to identify the causes of unitary tendencies in the working of the Constitution
It was to suggest measures securing the utmost autonomy for the States
It was to strengthen the Centre's control over education and health
n429992e4ff4.x: The committee sought to reduce central control, including over subjects such as education and health.

n1b4265820ba.s:
Assertion (A): The Rajamannar Committee found that central dominance had turned the States into 'administrative units of the Centre'.
Reason (R): The Committee identified Articles 280 and 282 as the main instruments of this overreach.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n1b4265820ba.x: A is true, but the Articles the Committee named as enabling overreach were 256, 257 and 365, not 280 and 282.

nad43318d9ab.s: The Rajamannar Committee recommended the immediate setting up of a permanent Inter-State Council under Article:
nad43318d9ab.x: Rajamannar wanted a permanent Inter-State Council under Article 263 at once, along with a revitalised Finance Commission.

n2c3eaeecda5.s: Dr. P.V. Rajamannar, chairman of the Centre-State Relations Inquiry Committee (1969), was a former Chief Justice of the ____ High Court.
n2c3eaeecda5.x: P.V. Rajamannar was a former Chief Justice of the Madras High Court; the committee was appointed in 1969 and reported in 1971.

nd618c01435c.s: Besides its Chairman, the members of the Rajamannar Committee were A. Lakshmanaswami Mudaliar and:
nd618c01435c.x: A. Lakshmanaswami Mudaliar and P. Chandra Reddy were the other two members; R.S. Sarkaria chaired a later commission.

nc12d7b88639.s: The Kurian Joseph Committee on Centre-State relations was appointed in:
nc12d7b88639.x: The Kurian Joseph Committee was appointed in April 2025, after Rajamannar (1969), Sarkaria (1983) and Punchhi (2007).

n5e2471a1a97.s: Which of the following was NOT a Sarkaria Commission recommendation on Article 356?
o: It should be used very sparingly, as a last resort
Loss of majority should be decided by the Governor's own assessment rather than a floor test
The State should be given a warning before it is invoked
Majority should be tested on the floor of the Assembly
n5e2471a1a97.x: Sarkaria wanted the majority tested by a floor test in the Assembly, not by the Governor's own assessment.

n584724d5aed.s: The courts relied on the Sarkaria report in S.R. Bommai (1994) and in:
n584724d5aed.x: Bommai and Rameshwar Prasad relied on Sarkaria; Kesavananda Bharati came a decade before the Commission.

nf886c4a0aee.s: The Sarkaria Commission recommended that a Governor should decide on Bills:
nf886c4a0aee.x: Sarkaria recommended strictly non-partisan appointment of Governors and decision on Bills within a specified period.

n499144acb01.s: Justice R.S. Sarkaria, who chaired the Commission on Centre-State relations, was a retired judge of the:
n499144acb01.x: Justice Rajinder Singh Sarkaria was a retired Supreme Court judge; his report made 247 recommendations.

n8f427351325.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Article 156 has been amended to remove the words 'during the pleasure of the President'
The 11th Inter-State Council meeting (16 July 2016) took up the Punchhi recommendations
The 11th Inter-State Council meeting was the first in about a decade
In State of Punjab v. Principal Secretary to the Governor (2023), the Supreme Court held a Governor cannot keep Bills pending indefinitely
n8f427351325.x: Article 156 is unchanged, so Governors still hold office during the pleasure of the President.

n8b630104f44.s: Which of the following was NOT a financial recommendation of the Punchhi Commission?
o: Time periods of the Finance and Planning Commissions should be synchronised with the Five Year Plans
Backward States should get higher central transfers with an area-specific strategy
Cesses and surcharges should be left unlimited
Cesses and surcharges should be limited
n8b630104f44.x: Punchhi wanted cesses and surcharges limited, not left unlimited.

nbca9826e54f.s:
Assertion (A): The Punchhi Commission recommended a constitutional amendment prescribing a six-month period for the Governor to decide on Bills passed by the State Assembly.
Reason (R): The Punchhi Commission preferred a Governor who had recently been active in local politics.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nbca9826e54f.x: A is true; R is false because Punchhi wanted an eminent person who had not been in active politics, even locally, for a couple of years before appointment.

na041d295d17.s: The Punchhi Commission on Centre-State relations was set up in:
na041d295d17.x: The UPA government set it up in April 2007; 2010 is the year of its report.

nceaf938297b.shape: one-liner (NOT not possible: all original statements are true)
nceaf938297b.s: In relation to Article 356, the NCRWC recommended:
o: Its use only on a Rajya Sabha resolution
nceaf938297b.x: The NCRWC sought safeguards against misuse of Article 356 (along with greater fiscal autonomy and a stronger third tier); deletion was Rajamannar's demand.

nfa4601db001.s: Which of the following Second ARC Report – subject pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Sixth Report – Capacity Building for Conflict Resolution
Seventh Report – Capacity Building for Conflict Resolution
Fifteenth Report – State and District Administration
nfa4601db001.x: The Sixth Report dealt with Local Governance; Capacity Building for Conflict Resolution was the Seventh Report.

n441b36f5441.s: A Code of Ethics, Right to Public Services laws and a Department of E-Governance were recommended by the:
n441b36f5441.x: The Second ARC recommended these, along with financial autonomy for PRIs and ULBs.

nf631da28dab.s: The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC) was chaired by:
nf631da28dab.x: M.N. Venkatachaliah chaired the NCRWC, which reported in 2002 after reviewing the Constitution's first 50 years.

n042ce93682a.s: The Indrajit Gupta Committee dealt with:
n042ce93682a.x: The Indrajit Gupta Committee dealt with electoral reform and State funding of elections, not Centre-State relations.

nindian-society-11-14.s: The Sri Krishna Commission, chaired by B.N. Srikrishna, inquired into the:
nindian-society-11-14.x: The Sri Krishna Commission inquired into the 1992–93 Mumbai riots.

n2a0ab5ad67a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about State-ranking indices?
o: The SDG India Index of NITI Aayog is now localised to districts
NITI Aayog prepares the Export Preparedness Index with the Institute for Competitiveness
Swachh Survekshan is released by NITI Aayog
Export infrastructure and export performance are pillars of the Export Preparedness Index
n2a0ab5ad67a.x: Swachh Survekshan is released by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, not NITI Aayog.

n21dc83675ab.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the structure of NITI Aayog?
o: Its CEO is a Union Cabinet Minister with no fixed tenure
The Prime Minister is its Chairperson and appoints the Vice-Chairperson
It can have at most two part-time members, by rotation
It can have at most four Union Ministers as ex-officio members
n21dc83675ab.x: The CEO of NITI Aayog is a Secretary-rank officer with a fixed tenure.

n1dfcd383119.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation
River boards are set up under the Inter-State Council Order, 1990
All five Zonal Councils are chaired by the Union Home Minister
Zonal Councils are statutory and advisory bodies
n1dfcd383119.x: River boards are set up under the River Boards Act, 1956.

n05f6965b374.s:
Assertion (A): The 2016 committee of Chief Ministers on digital payments was convened by N. Chandrababu Naidu.
Reason (R): It was one of the three NITI Aayog sub-groups constituted in 2015.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n05f6965b374.x: The digital-payments committee (2016, convened by Naidu) was separate from the three 2015 sub-groups, so R is false.

n864c58f6103.x: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission; it follows a bottom-up approach and has no power to allocate plan grants.

n7ffc783880f.s: The usual Centre-State funding ratio for core Centrally Sponsored Schemes is:
n7ffc783880f.x: The usual ratio is 60:40; for North-Eastern and Himalayan States it is 90:10.

n5ca3c1a1224.s: Which of the following Panchayat revenue source – basis pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Assigned taxes – State-levied taxes handed over to Panchayats
Shared taxes – Share of State taxes as recommended by the State Finance Commission
Grants-in-aid from the State Consolidated Fund – Article 280
n5ca3c1a1224.x: Grants from the State Consolidated Fund relate to Article 243H and State Finance Commission recommendations; Article 280 is the basis of Union Finance Commission grants.

n4eb17277134.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Fifteenth Finance Commission's tax devolution criteria?
o: Population, 2011 carried a weight of 15 per cent
Contribution to GDP was included as a criterion
Demographic performance carried a weight of 12.5 per cent
Tax and fiscal effort carried a weight of 2.5 per cent
n4eb17277134.x: Contribution to GDP was introduced by the Sixteenth Finance Commission, not the Fifteenth.

nd60b210abbf.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sixteenth Finance Commission (2026–31) devolution criteria?
o: Income distance has a weight of 42.5%
Contribution to GDP has been introduced with a weight of 10%
Tax and fiscal effort has been retained with a weight of 2.5%
nd60b210abbf.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission dropped the 2.5% tax and fiscal effort criterion.

n2d8dcfa4c9f.s:
Assertion (A): The 73rd Constitutional Amendment made reservation mandatory in Panchayati Raj institutions.
Reason (R): The 73rd Amendment also provided for State Finance Commissions.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n2d8dcfa4c9f.x: Both are true: the 73rd Amendment provided reservation and also State Finance Commissions, but providing SFCs does not explain the reservation.

n662140df410.s: The Fourteenth Finance Commission recommended vertical devolution of ____ of the divisible pool to the States.
n662140df410.x: The Fourteenth FC recommended 42 per cent; the Fifteenth and Sixteenth recommended 41 per cent.

n244db23d27f.s: Under the Fourteenth Finance Commission, the weight given to income distance was:
n244db23d27f.x: Income distance carried 50 per cent; population 1971 had 17.5, area 15 and forest cover 7.5 per cent.

nf76873ee377.s: Transfer of work to field officers within the bureaucracy, without transfer to elected local bodies, is called:
nf76873ee377.x: Administrative delegation or deconcentration keeps functions within the bureaucracy, whereas democratic decentralisation transfers power to elected local bodies.

nba14a9cdca5.s: Panchayats may levy taxes, duties, tolls and fees only when authorised by the State Legislature under Article:
nba14a9cdca5.x: Under Article 243H Panchayat taxing power depends on State legislative authorisation; property tax is a major own-source revenue.

n624746ac406.s: Under the Fourteenth Finance Commission, the basic-to-performance grant ratio for Gram Panchayats was:
n624746ac406.x: The Fourteenth FC used 90:10 for Gram Panchayats and 80:20 for Municipalities.

naa272ca523c.s: The Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program is a component of the:
naa272ca523c.x: The Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program and Training of Trainers on own-source revenue are associated with the revamped RGSA.

n5ccbf6e8fee.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about constitutional devolution to local bodies?
o: The Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules transfer subjects automatically without legislative action
These Articles say the State Legislature 'may' devolve powers and responsibilities
n5ccbf6e8fee.x: The Schedules do not transfer subjects automatically; Articles 243G and 243W use the discretionary 'may'.

nf1fa9f42cae.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about proxy representation of elected women in Panchayats?
o: 'Sarpanch pati' refers to a male relative exercising power in the elected woman's name
Proxy behaviour increases markedly when the woman enters a second term
Online trolling and intimidation are other problems faced by women leaders
Proxy behaviour falls markedly in a second term
nf1fa9f42cae.x: Proxy behaviour falls markedly, not increases, when the woman representative enters a second term.

nf5b592a099d.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Chief Election Commissioner – Removed like a High Court Judge
State Election Commissioner – Removed like a High Court Judge
State Election Commissioner – Appointed by the President
Elections to Municipalities – Conducted by the Election Commission of India
nf5b592a099d.x: Under Article 243K the State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor and removable only like a High Court Judge; the CEC is removed like a Supreme Court Judge.

nc6db5c3f6dd.s: In debates on local devolution, Janmabhoomi committees and secretariats are criticised as:
o: Parallel bodies weakening the centrality of PRIs
Constitutional planning bodies integrating local plans
nc6db5c3f6dd.x: The criticism is that PRIs act mainly as implementing agencies, while parallel bodies such as Janmabhoomi committees and secretariats reduce their centrality.

n29ccdf45af9.s: Which measure is identified as a response to proxy participation by male relatives in women-led Panchayats?
o: Conducting Panchayat meetings without elected representatives
Appointing Special Officers to run Panchayats
Exemplary penalties in proven proxy cases
n29ccdf45af9.x: Capacity building of elected women and exemplary penalties in proven proxy cases were identified as responses.

nafd95413a0d.s: Under the Sixteenth Finance Commission grants for 2026–31, the urban share increased from 36% to:
nafd95413a0d.x: The urban share rises to 45%, with grants split 80% basic and 20% performance.

n520836f08f1.s: The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet decision of 18 August 2026 provided ____ reservation for Backward Classes in rural local bodies.
n520836f08f1.x: It provided 34% BC reservation in rural local bodies and 33⅓% in urban local bodies, with direct election of Mayors and chairpersons.

n9d17d16f0b8.s: The Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan is aimed at:
o: Strengthening participation of elected women representatives
n9d17d16f0b8.x: Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan and Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats strengthen participation of elected women representatives.

ncebbb1ee1b3.s: Which constitutional arrangement ended the practice of postponing local elections at will?
o: Appointment of Special Officers for every local body
Elections held at the discretion of the State Government
A three-year term renewable by the State Government
A five-year term, with elections before expiry or within six months of dissolution, under the SEC
ncebbb1ee1b3.x: The five-year term with elections before expiry or within six months of dissolution, conducted by the State Election Commission, made local government a permanent institution after 1993.

nf3a90d65bb0.s: Village and ward secretariats and volunteers were introduced in Andhra Pradesh in:
nf3a90d65bb0.x: They were introduced in 2019, after the Janmabhoomi committees of 2014-19; both were criticised as parallel to gram panchayats and wards.

n7e90475fc57.s: Which of the following is identified as an arrangement that bypasses elected local bodies?
n7e90475fc57.x: DRDAs, user groups, SHGs and MPLADS/MLA LADS bypass elected local bodies; DPCs and MPCs are constitutional planning bodies.

n3faba5332fc.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: District Collector – District Election Officer/District Returning Officer
Election Commission of India – Conducts elections to Parliament and State Legislatures
Chief Electoral Officer – Conducts elections to Panchayats and municipalities
State Election Commission – Conducts elections to Panchayats and municipalities
n3faba5332fc.x: The Chief Electoral Officer is the State-level officer under the ECI's control; local-body elections are conducted by the State Election Commission.

nindian-polity-25-20.s: Which of the following elections is NOT conducted by the Election Commission of India?
nindian-polity-25-20.x: Panchayat elections at all three tiers are conducted by the State Election Commission.

n8f1f73d9db3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Chief Electoral Officer functions under the Representation of the People Act, 1950
The State Election Commission functions under Articles 243K and 243ZA
The Chief Electoral Officer is removed like a High Court judge
The State Election Commissioner is removable only like a High Court judge
n8f1f73d9db3.x: The Chief Electoral Officer is removed by the Election Commission; only the State Election Commissioner has High Court judge-like protection.

n45801048b27.shape: one-liner (NOT not possible: all original statements are true)
n45801048b27.s: The challenged composition of the Selection Committee under the 2023 Election Commission law gives the government a majority of:
n45801048b27.x: Petitions by ADR and Jaya Thakur challenge the 2:1 government majority; the Supreme Court said the CJI's place had been only temporary, pending a law.

nb9413396b7f.s:
Assertion (A): The Constitution places post-retirement restrictions on the CAG under Article 148(4).
Reason (R): The Constitution expressly bars retiring Election Commissioners from any further government appointment.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nb9413396b7f.x: A is true (as with the UPSC Chairman under Article 319), but the Constitution has no express bar for retiring Election Commissioners.

n3e10331c7fe.s: The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office:
o: In the same manner as a High Court judge
In the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge
By the President on the advice of the Prime Minister
On the recommendation of the Union Law Minister
n3e10331c7fe.x: The CEC is removable like a Supreme Court judge; Election Commissioners and Regional Commissioners only on the CEC's recommendation.

nindian-polity-25-21.s: The head of a State Election Commission can be removed only in the manner of a:
nindian-polity-25-21.x: A State Election Commissioner is removed like a High Court judge, while the CEC is removed like a Supreme Court judge.

n752c7ae678e.s: There is a demand that the expenses of the Election Commission of India be charged on the:
n752c7ae678e.x: Critics note the ECI's dependence on DoPT, Law and Home Ministries and demand its expenses be charged on the Consolidated Fund.

nf3725943f85.s: Which body decides every step of the election process, from the announcement of the schedule to the declaration of results?
nf3725943f85.x: The ECI decides every step from announcement to results; Panchayat and municipal polls belong to the State Election Commissions.

nindian-polity-25-16.s: An Election Commissioner holds office for six years or until attaining the age of ____, whichever is earlier.
nindian-polity-25-16.x: The ECI has one CEC and two ECs, appointed by the President, each serving six years or until age 65.

nindian-polity-25-5.s: The State Election Commission for municipal elections is provided under Article:
nindian-polity-25-5.x: Article 243ZA covers municipal elections; 243K covers Panchayat elections and 324 the ECI.

n543c2596969.s: The CEC and Election Commissioners receive equal salaries on a par with:
o: a judge of the Supreme Court
a judge of a High Court
n543c2596969.x: They are paid on a par with a Supreme Court judge, and their service conditions cannot be varied to their disadvantage.

ne84a03eb682.s: The Election Commission advises the Governor on disqualification of members of State Legislatures under Article:
ne84a03eb682.x: The ECI advises the Governor under Article 192 and the President under Article 103; anti-defection cases go to the Speaker or Chairman.

n8703fc8116d.s: The Tarkunde Committee on electoral reforms was set up by:
n8703fc8116d.x: Jayaprakash Narayan set up the Tarkunde Committee, which proposed a three-member Election Commission.

na72c54fb3e9.s: A challenge to an election result after it has been declared must be made through:
o: A review by the Election Commission
na72c54fb3e9.x: The Election Commission cannot review a declared result and does not try election petitions; challenges follow the election-petition route.

nd753e0154fc.s: V.S. Ramadevi, the first woman Chief Election Commissioner of India, served in:
nd753e0154fc.x: V.S. Ramadevi served as CEC in 1990; T.N. Seshan was the tenth CEC.

n8bb45ed2a59.s: National Voters' Day, observed since 2011, falls every year on:
n8bb45ed2a59.x: National Voters' Day is 25 January, the ECI's foundation day (25 January 1950).

nabf2e8c7053.s: Under Article 324(1), the ECI's superintendence does NOT extend to elections to:
nabf2e8c7053.x: Article 324(1) covers Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President; Panchayat and municipal polls come under the State Election Commissions.

n73532628ae2.s: The 2022 delimitation of Jammu and Kashmir was conducted by a Commission headed by Justice:
n73532628ae2.x: The J&K delimitation (2022) was done by a Commission under Justice Ranjana Desai, while Assam was delimited by the ECI.

necc3f676a93.s: The Search Committee for Election Commissioners under the 2023 Act is headed by the:
necc3f676a93.x: The Search Committee is headed by the Law Minister, has two Secretary-rank members and shortlists five names.

n5c42066acdd.s: Article 324, which provides for the Election Commission of India, lies in Part ____ of the Constitution.

n3334f7418d0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the election machinery?
o: The Election Commission has no control over officers deployed on poll duty
The Chief Electoral Officer assists the Election Commission in each State or UT
Electoral Registration Officers and Booth Level Officers are associated with electoral rolls
Booth Level Officers now carry standard photo identity cards
n3334f7418d0.x: The Election Commission controls officers on poll duty and may transfer them or act against partisan conduct.

nindian-polity-22-41.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Representation of the People Act, 1950 – Allocation of seats and preparation of electoral rolls
Representation of the People Act, 1951 – Conduct of elections and disqualification of members
Article 171 – Superintendence, direction and control of elections by the Election Commission
nindian-polity-22-41.x: Article 171 deals with the composition of State Legislative Councils; superintendence of elections is vested in the ECI by Article 324.

n199802edea4.shape: one-liner (NOT not possible: all original statements are true)
n199802edea4.s: The grounds for declaring an election void are listed in which Section of the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
n199802edea4.x: Section 100 lists grounds such as disqualification of the returned candidate, corrupt practice and improper rejection of a nomination.

n8b6fe9cf089.s: Which of the following ECI initiative – purpose pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: SVEEP – Voter education and electoral participation
cVIGIL – Assistance and facilities for voters with disabilities
Saksham – Assistance and facilities for voters with disabilities
Voter Helpline – Registration, corrections, roll search and complaints
n8b6fe9cf089.x: cVIGIL is for reporting Model Code violations through geo-tagged photographs or videos; Saksham assists voters with disabilities.

n845ce618199.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about women's reservation under the 106th Amendment?
o: It operates immediately, irrespective of census and delimitation
It provides one-third reservation of seats
n845ce618199.x: Its operation begins only after the next census and delimitation.

nf546ff8f15e.s: Which of the following Representation of the People Act, 1951 Section – content pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Section 80 – No election may be called in question except by an election petition
Section 81 – Election petition to be tried by the High Court
Section 100 – Grounds for declaring an election void
nf546ff8f15e.x: Section 81 prescribes presenting the petition within 45 days; trial by the High Court is under Section 80A.

nindian-polity-53-23.s: Recognition of political parties and reservation of symbols is governed by the:
nindian-polity-53-23.x: The 1968 Order recognises parties and reserves symbols; the RPA 1950 covers seats and rolls, and the RPA 1951 nomination, scrutiny and counting.

na5e4dcc1c47.s: For State Party recognition on seat share, a party needs three per cent of Assembly seats or ____ seats, whichever is more.
na5e4dcc1c47.x: One alternative criterion is three per cent of Assembly seats or three seats, whichever is more.

n96fea97b16a.s: In a constituency reserved for Scheduled Castes, who can vote?
o: Only voters belonging to Scheduled Castes
Only voters belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
Only voters belonging to Scheduled Castes and Backward Classes
n96fea97b16a.x: Reserved constituencies have a common electorate: all voters, not merely those of the reserved community, may vote.

nindian-polity-36-16.s: The voting age was lowered from 21 to 18 years by the:
nindian-polity-36-16.x: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 lowered the voting age to 18.

nindian-polity-66-27.s: NOTA is NOT applicable in which of the following elections?
nindian-polity-66-27.x: NOTA does not apply to Rajya Sabha or Legislative Council elections.

nindian-polity-66-10.s: A candidate forfeits the security deposit on securing not more than ____ of the valid votes.
nindian-polity-66-10.x: A candidate with one-sixth or less of the valid votes forfeits the deposit.

n38f2118ecaa.s: The 84th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2001 permitted rationalisation of constituencies on the basis of the ____ Census.
n38f2118ecaa.x: The 84th Amendment extended the freeze on inter-State seat allocation and allowed rationalisation using the 1991 Census.

nindian-polity-53-43.s: Disqualifications for membership of Parliament are dealt with in Article:
nindian-polity-53-43.x: Article 102 covers disqualifications for Parliament; 84 its qualifications, 173 and 191 those for State Legislatures.

n2f91d4c5244.s: The number of Scheduled Caste-reserved seats in the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly is:
n2f91d4c5244.x: Andhra Pradesh has 29 SC and 7 ST Assembly seats; Telangana has 19 SC and 12 ST.

nfd928c56503.s: For a Lok Sabha general election, the notification under Section 14 of the RPA 1951 is issued by the:
nfd928c56503.x: The President notifies Lok Sabha polls on the ECI's recommendation; the ECI fixes the schedule and nomination dates.

nindian-polity-36-7.s: The Vice-President of India is elected by:
nindian-polity-36-7.x: The Vice-President is elected by all MPs, elected and nominated, by single transferable vote; the President by elected MPs and MLAs.

nc81d76bcee0.s: The authority of the Model Code of Conduct is associated with the Election Commission's plenary power under Article:
nc81d76bcee0.x: The Model Code is a set of ECI guidelines supported by Article 324, not a statute enacted by Parliament.

nindian-polity-40-3.s: The constitutional authority for conducting State Legislative Assembly elections is the:
nindian-polity-40-3.x: Assembly elections are direct, use first-past-the-post and are run by the Election Commission of India.

nd41691c82f4.s: Under Section 78 of the RPA 1951, election expense accounts must be filed with the District Election Officer within:
nd41691c82f4.x: Section 78 requires expense accounts to reach the DEO, usually the Collector, within 30 days.

n179c12cb096.s: Election expense accounts are dealt with in which Sections of the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
n179c12cb096.x: Sections 77–78 of the 1951 Act cover election expenses; Section 8 covers disqualifications.

nindian-polity-53-29.s: The Delimitation Commission is headed by a:
nindian-polity-53-29.x: It is set up under an Act of Parliament, headed by a retired Supreme Court judge, with the CEC and State Election Commissioners as members.

nindian-polity-66-8.s: Under the old Rule 49-O, a voter:
o: Pressed the NOTA button on the EVM
Voided the result by majority rejection
Entered the booth but refused to vote before the Presiding Officer
nindian-polity-66-8.x: Old Rule 49-O meant refusing to vote before the presiding officer; NOTA means pressing a button on the EVM.

n9163be7803c.s: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 proposed raising the Lok Sabha ceiling from 550 to:
n9163be7803c.x: The Bill proposed 850 seats with delimitation on the 2011 Census, but it was defeated.

n90789c4cecc.s: An election held after a legislature is dissolved before the expiry of its normal term is called a:
n90789c4cecc.x: A mid-term election follows premature dissolution; a by-election fills a single vacancy, ordinarily within six months.

n16eb65cf256.s: Which Lok Sabha constituency in Andhra Pradesh is reserved for Scheduled Tribes?
n16eb65cf256.x: Araku is the ST-reserved constituency; Amalapuram and Tirupati are SC-reserved.

n6a9b6eeb6f4.s: The 17th Lok Sabha was elected in:
n6a9b6eeb6f4.x: The 17th Lok Sabha was elected in 2019; 2014 elected the 16th and 2024 the 18th.

nf8cb10f42a1.s: Persons in preventive detention may vote through:
o: A special booth in the jail
nf8cb10f42a1.x: Persons in preventive detention, along with service voters, special voters and electors on election duty, are covered by postal-ballot provisions.

n584fd7ea925.s: Reservation of one-third of seats for women, under the 106th Amendment, is linked to Article:
n584fd7ea925.x: Article 334A relates to the women's one-third reservation; Article 330 covers SC/ST seats in the Lok Sabha and 331 the former Anglo-Indian nomination.

n7685c768c75.s: Under first-past-the-post in Lok Sabha elections, a candidate wins by securing:
o: More than half of the valid votes
At least one-third of the valid votes
At least two-thirds of the valid votes
n7685c768c75.x: FPTP needs only a plurality in a single-member constituency, not a majority.

ncbc22496fc5.s: A party is eligible for National Party recognition if it is recognised as a State party in at least ____ States.
ncbc22496fc5.x: State-party recognition in four or more States is one of the alternative criteria under the Election Symbols Order, 1968.

ncb99b5c45d0.s: The Model Code of Conduct was first drafted and used in the 1960 Assembly election of:
ncb99b5c45d0.x: The Code was first used in Kerala in 1960, formalised by the ECI in 1968 and strictly enforced by T.N. Seshan in 1991.

n417d9aa690e.s: The Delimitation Commission is constituted under:
o: An executive order of the President
A notification of the Election Commission
A resolution of the Rajya Sabha
n417d9aa690e.x: It is constituted under parliamentary legislation, works with the ECI, and its orders cannot be modified by the Lok Sabha or Assemblies.

n8a567566d37.s: The key chemical in the indelible ink used in Indian elections is:
n8a567566d37.x: Silver nitrate is the key chemical; the formula comes from the National Physical Laboratory and it is applied on the left forefinger.

nc0739af5e1e.s: IIIDEM, which trains election managers, is an institute of the:
nc0739af5e1e.x: IIIDEM belongs to the Election Commission, a permanent independent constitutional body constituted in 1950.

nindian-polity-25-8.s: In the Kuldip Nayar case (2006), the Supreme Court held the right to vote to be a:
nindian-polity-25-8.x: Kuldip Nayar held the right to vote statutory, not fundamental.

nindian-polity-36-36.s: The Vice-President is elected under Article:
nindian-polity-36-36.x: The Vice-President is elected under Article 66; the President under Article 54.

nindian-polity-53-22.s: Corrupt practices in elections are dealt with in the:
nindian-polity-53-22.x: Corrupt practices and disqualifications are in the RPA, 1951; voter registration is in the 1950 Act.

nindian-polity-25-33.s: Article 83, which may need amending for simultaneous elections, deals with the:
o: Duration of the Houses of Parliament
nindian-polity-25-33.x: Articles 83 and 85 concern Parliament's term and sessions, 172 and 174 the States', and 356 President's Rule; all may need amending.

nindian-polity-60-3.s: A candidate can win a State Assembly election without obtaining more than 50 per cent of the votes because Assembly elections follow the:
o: Proportional representation by single transferable vote
nindian-polity-60-3.x: Under first-past-the-post, the candidate with the most valid votes wins even without 50 per cent.

nindian-polity-66-23.s: Former Rule 49-O was struck down because recording a voter's refusal to vote in Form ____ compromised secrecy.
nindian-polity-66-23.x: Recording the refusal in Form 17-A broke the secrecy of the vote.

nindian-polity-66-3.s: The right to register a secret negative vote (NOTA) was linked by the Supreme Court to Article:
nindian-polity-66-3.x: The Court linked a secret negative vote to freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a).

ned0ca584baf.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Tarkunde Committee on electoral reforms?
o: It was appointed in 1974 and reported in 1975
It proposed a selection panel of the Prime Minister, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Chief Justice of India
It was set up by Jayaprakash Narayan
It recommended a three-member Election Commission and a voting age of 18
ned0ca584baf.x: The proposed panel was the PM, the Leader of the Opposition and the CJI, not the Speaker.

n7fdda51ac60.shape: one-liner (NOT not possible: all original statements are true)
n7fdda51ac60.s: Linking of electoral rolls with Aadhaar to check multiple enrolment was provided by the:
o: Representation of the People Act, 1950 as originally enacted
n7fdda51ac60.x: The Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021 provided Aadhaar linking, multiple qualifying dates, gender-neutral wording and requisition of premises.

naae0157627d.shape: one-liner (NOT not possible: all original statements are true)
naae0157627d.s: Under ADR v. ECI (2024), symbol-loading units are to be sealed and preserved for:
naae0157627d.x: The Court rejected ballot papers and 100% VVPAT counting, but ordered SLUs preserved for 45 days and allowed runners-up to seek checking of 5% of EVMs.

nb6ab69977e5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about judgments on criminalisation of politics?
o: Public Interest Foundation (2018) left disqualification on framing of charges to Parliament
Public Interest Foundation (2018) ordered publicity of candidates' criminal records
In Public Interest Foundation (2018), the Court itself imposed disqualification on framing of charges
Lily Thomas removed protection from disqualification during pendency of an appeal
nb6ab69977e5.x: The Court did not itself impose disqualification on framing of charges; it left the issue to Parliament.

n6243d9bfbba.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about VVPAT?
o: It is attached to the Electronic Voting Machine
It prints a slip with the serial number, name and symbol of the selected candidate
The voter can see the printed slip for seven seconds
The slip is handed over to the voter for personal custody
n6243d9bfbba.x: The voter only views the slip through the VVPAT window; it is not handed over.

nindian-polity-73-12.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Parur Assembly Constituency – First experimental use of EVM
Goa (1999) – First State-wide Assembly election using EVMs
14th Lok Sabha election (2004) – First nationwide general election entirely using EVMs
nindian-polity-73-12.x: VVPAT was first introduced in Noksen Assembly Constituency; Goa saw the first all-EVM State poll.

nindian-polity-28-4.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Sarkaria Commission – Recommendation for a permanent Inter-State Council
Punchhi Commission – State-level initiative for federal autonomy
Rajamannar Committee – State-level initiative for federal autonomy
Indrajit Gupta Committee – State funding of elections
nindian-polity-28-4.x: Punchhi dealt with federal dialogue and coordination mechanisms; the State-level autonomy initiative was Rajamannar (Tamil Nadu).

n1fe38e89a68.s: Under Section 8 of the RPA 1951, conviction resulting in imprisonment of ____ or more attracts disqualification.
n1fe38e89a68.x: Section 8 disqualifies on conviction with two years' imprisonment or more; Lily Thomas removed protection during pendency of an appeal.

neba772ed4bf.s: The reform principle 'one candidate, one seat' addresses:
o: Candidates contesting from more than one constituency
neba772ed4bf.x: The Law Commission proposed 'one candidate, one seat' for candidates contesting from more than one constituency; the ECI proposed the vacating candidate bear by-election costs.

nf2842a71a56.s: In the 2024 electoral bond judgment, the Supreme Court directed ____ to provide donor data to the Election Commission.
nf2842a71a56.x: A five-judge Constitution Bench unanimously struck down the scheme and directed SBI to provide donor data to the ECI.

nf872a3ef75d.s: Mandatory disclosure by candidates of criminal cases, assets, liabilities and education was laid down in:
o: Lily Thomas v. Union of India
Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India
Public Interest Foundation v. Union of India
nf872a3ef75d.x: ADR (2002) made such disclosure mandatory; PUCL placed the voter's right to know in Article 19(1)(a).

n2d416038b69.s: The Law Commission report that recommended giving the ECI a limited power to deregister non-compliant parties is the:
n2d416038b69.x: The 255th Report (2015) sought limited deregistration power; the 170th Report (1999) dealt with internal party democracy and partial list seats.

nc857cc77580.s: The 'level field for resource-poor candidates' argument for State funding of elections rests on equality under Article:
nc857cc77580.x: The level-field argument rests on equality under Article 14; curbing black money is another argument in favour, while the fiscal burden is an argument against.

nc191234fd0c.s: Under the ECI's requirement, political parties fielding candidates with criminal records must publish the details of those records and:
o: The reasons for selecting such candidates
An undertaking to resign if convicted
nc191234fd0c.x: Parties must publish the criminal-record details and the reasons for selecting such candidates; withdrawal is not required.

na6776d883fb.s: A person elected from two constituencies must vacate one of them within:
na6776d883fb.x: Under Section 70 one seat must be vacated within 14 days; the two-constituency cap in Section 33(7) came with the 1996 amendment.

na44b6c2c3f9.s: The Electors' Photo Identity Card (EPIC) was introduced in:
na44b6c2c3f9.x: EPIC was introduced in 1993 and its number stays valid for life despite a change of address; it did not come through the 61st Amendment.

n5b0a369112f.s: Under Section 34 of the RPA 1951, the security deposit for a general-category Lok Sabha candidate is:
n5b0a369112f.x: It is ₹25,000 for the Lok Sabha and ₹10,000 for an Assembly; SC/ST candidates pay half.

nc36f21173b7.s: The current election expenditure limit for a Lok Sabha candidate in a larger State is:
nc36f21173b7.x: The limit is ₹95 lakh (earlier ₹70 lakh), raised by the Conduct of Elections (Amendment) Rules, 2022; ₹40 lakh is the Assembly limit.

n25cf1d6ee5a.s: A State funding model in which the State bears all legitimate costs and private donations are banned is:
n25cf1d6ee5a.x: Bearing all legitimate costs while banning private donations describes full funding; funding may be full or partial, in cash or in kind.

n242b09ddcba.s: A totaliser, which combines the counting of several EVMs, is intended to:
n242b09ddcba.x: A totaliser combines several EVM counts to hide booth-wise trends; the ECI stated no legal framework for it exists.

nbb92f07bf72.s: ECIL, one of the two public sector undertakings that manufacture EVMs, is headquartered in:
nbb92f07bf72.x: BEL is based in Bengaluru and ECIL in Hyderabad.

n377a64cc072.s: Simultaneous Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections were held from 1951-52 up to:
n377a64cc072.x: Simultaneous polls were held from 1951-52 to 1967; both the 170th Law Commission Report and the 2018 draft report backed them.

n46020bbc32f.s: The High-Level Committee on simultaneous elections (2023-24) was chaired by:
n46020bbc32f.x: Former President Ram Nath Kovind chaired it; Amit Shah and N.K. Singh were members, and Dinesh Goswami headed the 1990 electoral reform committee.

n7ec8b7d2178.s: Which Article is NOT among those the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 proposes to amend?
n7ec8b7d2178.x: The Bill proposes amendments to Articles 83, 172 and 327, not Article 280.

nb995aabceb8.s: The Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) recommended State funding of elections in the form of:
o: Partial funding in kind to recognised parties and candidates
Full funding in cash to every candidate
Full funding in kind to every candidate
Partial cash funding to independents only
nb995aabceb8.x: It suggested partial funding in kind to recognised parties and candidates; the recommendation is still not adopted.

nindian-polity-54-18.s: Which of the following party – year of formation pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
nindian-polity-54-18.x: The CPI dates from 1925; the BJP (1980), BSP (1984), SP (1992), TMC (1998) and NCP (1999) were formed in 1980 or later.

n765043e1ef0.s:
Assertion (A): Following INC v. Institute of Social Welfare (2002), the Election Commission cannot ordinarily deregister a political party.
Reason (R): Deregistration may be possible in cases of fraud or where a party is declared unlawful.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n765043e1ef0.x: Both are true: the decision restricted the ECI's deregistration power, while recognising exceptions; the exceptions do not explain the general restriction.

nindian-polity-54-5.s: The first President of the Indian National Congress was:
nindian-polity-54-5.x: W.C. Banerjee was the Congress's first president; Syama Prasad Mookerjee founded the Jana Sangh and Vajpayee was the BJP's first president.

na461f71bab7.s: The first national party from the North-East is the:
na461f71bab7.x: The National People's Party was the first national party from the North-East; AAP got national-party status in 2023.

n0a1ff0bbbd3.s: The multi-party coalition era of the Indian party system covers the period:
n0a1ff0bbbd3.x: The Congress system covered 1952–77, the first alternation 1977–89, the coalition era 1989–2014, and the BJP majority phase began in 2014.

n7947b56b8fd.s: The Vohra Committee (1993) is associated with:
n7947b56b8fd.x: The Vohra Committee (1993) dealt with the criminalisation of politics.

n0f8670e1f9c.s: Puchalapalli Sundarayya was secretary of the Andhra Communist Party formed at ____ in 1936.
n0f8670e1f9c.x: Sundarayya was secretary of the Andhra Communist Party at Kakinada (1936).

nd692a46c66e.s: Pressure groups are described as the:
nd692a46c66e.x: Pressure groups, which seek influence rather than power, are called the 'Anonymous Empire'.

n142ee1b4605.s: The Bahujan Samaj Party was founded in 1984 by:
n142ee1b4605.x: Kanshi Ram founded the BSP (1984); Mulayam Singh Yadav founded the Samajwadi Party (1992).

nc423534971e.s: A political party must apply for registration under Section 29A of the RPA 1951 within ____ of its formation.
nc423534971e.x: The application must be made within 30 days of formation.

nindian-polity-54-4.s: The Communist Party of India was founded in:
nindian-polity-54-4.x: The CPI dates from 1925; the CPI(M) emerged after the 1964 split.

nb195dc2bf22.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: National Democratic Alliance – National Common Minimum Programme (2004)
National Front (1989–90) – Headed by V.P. Singh
United Front (1996–98) – Prime Ministers Deve Gowda and Gujral
nb195dc2bf22.x: The NDA adopted the National Agenda for Governance (1998); the National Common Minimum Programme (2004) was the UPA's.

nb1193a7e7de.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about State coalition governments after the 1967 elections?
o: Tamil Nadu too was ruled by a coalition of opposition parties
They were known as Samyukta Vidhayak Dal governments
Rich and middle peasants defecting from the Congress contributed to their rise
In Tamil Nadu the DMK ruled alone
nb1193a7e7de.x: Tamil Nadu was the exception, where the DMK ruled alone.

n9b504aa3c27.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about registered-unrecognised political parties?
o: They form a very large segment of India's registered parties
All of them contested the 2024 general election
Only about 750 of them contested the 2024 general election
n9b504aa3c27.x: Only about 750 of the over 2,800 registered-unrecognised parties contested the 2024 general election.

n36b5acaddbb.s: By Election Commission status, political parties are classified as national parties, State parties and:
n36b5acaddbb.x: The ECI categories are national, State and registered-unrecognised parties; cadre and mass parties are an organisational classification.

n766ed3e802c.s: In the 11th Lok Sabha (1996), the BJP emerged as the largest party with ____ seats.
n766ed3e802c.x: In 1996 the BJP won 161 and the INC 140; 182 was the BJP's 1999 tally and 85 its 1989 tally.

n0cd29693259.s: The United Front governments (1996–98) were headed successively by H.D. Deve Gowda and:
n0cd29693259.x: Deve Gowda and I.K. Gujral headed the United Front governments, which had outside Congress support.

nc53faefb4ec.s: The National Front government of 1989-90 was headed by:
nc53faefb4ec.x: V.P. Singh headed the minority National Front government, which survived on outside support from the BJP and the Left.

n1a1d49934ef.s: Congress dominance of the Andhra Pradesh party system continued until:
n1a1d49934ef.x: Congress dominance lasted until 1983; then the contest was Congress vs TDP, and since 2014 TDP vs YSR Congress.

ne6fc0d311c4.s: In Andhra Pradesh's current coalition arrangement, the Bharatiya Janata Party is:
o: A supporting partner of a dominant regional party
In opposition to the ruling coalition
ne6fc0d311c4.x: The arrangement is a coalition in which a regional party is the dominant partner and the BJP supports it.

n2719dd1ef08.s:
Assertion (A): After 1989, coalition arithmetic increased the weight of regional parties in India.
Reason (R): Uniform economic development across all regions is among the causes of the rise of regional parties.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n2719dd1ef08.x: A is true; R is false because regional economic neglect, not uniform development, fuels regional parties.

n1c350449942.s: N.T. Rama Rao founded the Telugu Desam Party in 1982 on the plank of:
n1c350449942.x: NTR founded the TDP on Telugu self-respect and won power in January 1983; it had no specific ideology beyond Telugu pride and welfare populism.

nc3e59d4e5f8.s: Critics fear that 'One Nation, One Election' would:
o: Increase the number of regional parties
Reduce the role of national parties
nc3e59d4e5f8.x: The fear is that it would weaken regional parties, not increase them.

n8663df2d940.s: The TDP left the NDA over the Special Category Status demand for Andhra Pradesh in:
n8663df2d940.x: The SCS demand concerned residuary AP after 2014; the TDP left the NDA over it in 2018.

n25b27962fb0.s: The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) was founded in:
n25b27962fb0.x: The DMK was founded in 1949, before the Shiv Sena (1966), TDP (1982) and BSP (1984).

nindian-polity-25-26.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Deciding disputes between rival groups of a recognised party – Quasi-judicial decision of the ECI
Disqualification of a Member of Parliament – President, acting on the binding opinion of the ECI
Grounds for declaring an election void – Section 100, RPA 1951
Registration of political parties – Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968
nindian-polity-25-26.x: Parties are registered under Section 29A of the RPA, 1951; the Symbols Order, 1968 governs allotment of symbols.

ne42b1e56c54.s:
Assertion (A): The Election Commission's power to deregister a political party is limited.
Reason (R): Fraud may form a basis for deregistration of a party.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
ne42b1e56c54.x: Both are true: the power is limited and arises in cases such as fraud or ceasing allegiance, but fraud being a ground does not explain why the power is limited.

n942786d4ac2.s: Under Section 29A, a party's constitution must pledge allegiance to the Constitution and to:
n942786d4ac2.x: It must pledge allegiance to the Constitution and to socialism, secularism, democracy and national integrity; a reserved symbol comes only with recognition.

nb6adc8019f4.s: One route to State-party recognition is at least 6% of valid votes in the Assembly election plus ____ Assembly seats.
nb6adc8019f4.x: The route is 6% plus 2 Assembly seats (or 6% in the Lok Sabha poll plus 1 Lok Sabha seat); '6% + 4 Lok Sabha seats' belongs to the National-party criterion.

n883a08b76a7.s: For State-party recognition, the 8% valid-vote route requires the party to win:
n883a08b76a7.x: The 8% route requires no seat; any one of the prescribed routes suffices.

n7554468f756.s: Under the Election Symbols Order, 1968, free symbols are meant for:
n7554468f756.x: Reserved symbols go only to recognised parties; free symbols are for registered unrecognised parties and independents.

nindian-polity-53-42.s: Under one route to National Party status, a party must win 2% of Lok Sabha seats (11 seats) from at least ____ States.
nindian-polity-53-42.x: The MPs must come from at least three States, not four.

n107869a4a10.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about removal of members of Public Service Commissions?
o: Insolvency is a ground for removal
Misbehaviour can be established by the President without referring the matter to the Supreme Court
Paid employment outside the duties of office is a ground for removal
Infirmity of mind or body is a ground for removal
n107869a4a10.x: In a case of misbehaviour, the President must first refer the matter to the Supreme Court.

n734a647956b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about a Joint State Public Service Commission?
o: Its Chairman and members are appointed by the President
Their service conditions and number are fixed by the President
A member submits resignation to the concerned Governor
The term is six years or until the age of 62, whichever is earlier
n734a647956b.x: A member of a Joint Commission resigns to the President, not to the Governor.

ne9bc8ba31c0.s:
Assertion (A): A member of a Joint State Public Service Commission retires at the age of 65 years.
Reason (R): A member of a State Public Service Commission holds office for six years or until the age of 62, whichever is earlier.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
ne9bc8ba31c0.x: The age limit for a Joint State PSC member is 62, not 65, so A is false; R is true (UPSC members retire at 65).

n8ec345d861e.s: The annual report of a State Public Service Commission is submitted to the:
n8ec345d861e.x: An SPSC reports to the Governor, who lays it before the State Legislature; the UPSC reports to the President.

n6f6fa187634.s: The APPSC came into existence on 1 November 1956 by merging the Andhra PSC (1953) with the ____ PSC.
n6f6fa187634.x: APPSC merged the Andhra PSC (1953) with the Hyderabad PSC; after 2014 it continues for residuary AP, while Telangana got the TSPSC.

nindian-polity-52-12.s: The Lokpal Selection Committee is chaired by the:
nindian-polity-52-12.x: The Prime Minister chairs the Lokpal Selection Committee; the President appoints the UPSC Chairman and the Governor the SPSC Chairman.

n9b4d2b9d3dc.s: The provisions on Public Service Commissions (Articles 315-323) are in Part ____ of the Constitution.
n9b4d2b9d3dc.x: Articles 315-323 are in Part XIV; the UPSC is a constitutional body, not a statutory one.

ndd0511a3791.s: On the Lee Commission's recommendation, a Public Service Commission was first set up in India on:
ndd0511a3791.x: The Lee Commission recommended it in 1924 and it was set up on 1 October 1926; the Federal PSC became the UPSC on 26 January 1950.

n35b3653a69a.s: A member of a State Public Service Commission addresses the resignation to the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
n35b3653a69a.x: An SPSC member resigns to the Governor; UPSC and JSPSC members resign to the President. Removal is only by the President.

n82cebf74fd6.s: Which of the following is ordinarily subject to consultation with the UPSC?
o: Claims of SCs and STs to services and posts
Temporary appointments for less than one year
Group B and Group C posts
Temporary appointments for more than one year
n82cebf74fd6.x: Temporary appointments exceeding one year are ordinarily subject to consultation; the other three are excluded.

n824c6eae955.s: Regulations excluding posts from consultation with a Public Service Commission must be laid before the legislature for at least:
n824c6eae955.x: The President (Governor for an SPSC) may exclude posts by regulations, which are laid for 14 days, not 30.

nbd9d09173c7.s: Under Article 321, the functions of the UPSC can be extended by:
o: An executive order of the President
A resolution of the Rajya Sabha
nbd9d09173c7.x: Functions are extended only by an Act of Parliament (State Legislature for an SPSC), which may cover local bodies, corporate bodies and public institutions.
